propositions: Recovery preflight refuses contexts over 100k chars even when the product (context_chars × criteria_count) is within the previously ratified worst-case budget of 3.2M chars
The flat per-context bound of 100k chars conflates two distinct ceilings: physical (fit one evidence run in the model window) and economic (per-criterion fan-out multiplier)
Context bounds must derive from the resolved verifier model's actual window size rather than a hardcoded constant, enabling contexts to scale with model capability
The economic ceiling should be expressed as a product limit (3.2M chars = context × criteria) instead of arbitrary per-axis splits, allocating headroom where real tickets need it
The live c9f7 ticket (121,147 chars context, 22 criteria, 2.67M char product) is blocked at preflight despite fitting under the ratified worst case due to the per-axis bound mismatch
Window-derived ceiling with conservative 2 chars/token ratio and interim product limit unblocks re-certifications while preserving the no-elision invariant and zero pre-verdict billing
